Germany, Austria and Switzerland reward brands that earn trust: demanding users, strict regulation and a media scene that reads the fine print. We build your go-to-market around exactly that – from positioning to PR, KOLs, content and partnerships – and run it hands-on until it works.

How we work (5 steps):
1. Audit & market fit: We map your category in DACH: competitors, narratives, search demand, the media and creator landscape and regulatory touchpoints. The result: where you can win – and where you shouldn’t spend a single euro.
2. Positioning & GTM plan: We sharpen your message for German-speaking users and turn it into a channel plan with clear priorities, KPIs and a launch roadmap that fits your product and your regulatory status.
3. Launch: PR, KOLs, content and partnerships go live together – timed so that every channel amplifies the others. One team, one plan, one voice in German.
4. Optimize & scale: We track what drives sign-ups and revenue, double down on what works and cut what doesn’t – from creator mix to partnerships and community.
5. Expand across Europe: Once your DACH playbook works, we take it to France, Spain and Italy through our network – and launch campaigns there right away.

Why Germany: Europe’s largest economy and one of its biggest crypto markets – the perfect place to prove your product in Europe. We know how to win it. Test: 100M+ German speakers across DACH. Demanding users, strict regulation – if it works here, it works across Europe. Win: Not one channel, but the right mix – PR, KOLs, content, partnerships and community, launched fast and working together from every angle. Scale: Ready to go big? Our network in France, Spain and Italy lets us launch campaigns there right away.

Homepage FAQ:
Q: What does MarketWerk do?
A: MarketWerk is a boutique go-to-market agency for international crypto brands entering Germany and the wider DACH market (Germany, Austria, Switzerland). We combine strategy with hands-on execution across PR, KOL and influencer marketing, German content and SEO, partnerships and community – and run it with you until it delivers.

Q: Why should a crypto brand start in Germany?
A: Germany is Europe’s largest economy and one of its biggest crypto markets. Together with Austria and Switzerland, DACH counts 100M+ German speakers. Users are demanding and regulation is strict – if your product wins here, it is ready for the rest of Europe. Our DACH market comparison explains the differences between the three countries.

Q: Which companies do you work with?
A: International crypto brands that want to grow in the German-speaking market – brands like Waltio, ether.fi, Blever, Nest Collective and Anon Summit. Read how we took Waltio into the German market. In the intro call we decide together whether we are the right fit.

Q: How is crypto marketing regulated in Germany?
A: Since 30 December 2024 the EU’s MiCA regulation applies in full: marketing communications must be identifiable as marketing, fair, clear and not misleading, and consistent with any white paper. In Germany BaFin is the competent authority, and influencer posts must be labelled as advertising. We plan campaigns with these rules in mind and coordinate with your legal counsel – details in our MiCA marketing guide.

Q: How fast can we launch?
A: That depends on your product, your regulatory status and the assets you already have. In the intro call we clarify scope and priorities, and the plan sets out what goes live first. For reference: the Waltio go-to-market ran over 6–8 months and delivered 70+ media publications and a #3 organic ranking for crypto tax topics within a few months.

Q: What does it cost?
A: Every engagement is scoped to your goals and markets – a single channel costs less than a full go-to-market. After a free intro call you receive a concrete proposal with scope, deliverables and budget, so you can decide with all the facts on the table.

Q: Do you only work in DACH?
A: DACH is our home turf, not our limit. Through our network in France, Spain and Italy we can launch campaigns there right away – ideally once your German playbook works. See how we plan a go-to-market strategy that scales.

# Services
## Go-to-Market Strategy – https://marketwerk.com/services/crypto-go-to-market-strategy/
We turn your market entry into a plan you can run: market and competitor analysis, positioning, channel mix and a launch roadmap for Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

At a glance:
- MarketWerk builds go-to-market strategies for international crypto brands entering Germany, Austria and Switzerland (DACH).
- The work covers market and competitor analysis, positioning, a regulatory-readiness check with the client's legal counsel, the channel mix and a launch roadmap along Test → Win → Scale.
- For the French crypto tax tool Waltio, MarketWerk built and ran the German go-to-market and helped the team find out within a couple of months whether Waltio could reach product-market fit in Germany.

A crypto go-to-market strategy for Germany defines who you target, what you say, which channels you use in which order and how you measure traction – before the launch budget is spent. Germany is Europe's largest economy and one of its biggest crypto markets. Together with Austria and Switzerland, it gives you 100M+ German speakers to test on.

It is also a market that punishes copy-paste launches. DACH users read the fine print, prefer regulated providers and expect German-language support plus transparency on fees, security and regulation. Major ad platforms restrict crypto ads, and MiCA requires marketing communications to be fair, clear and not misleading. In many categories, local incumbents already own the brand recognition, the search rankings and the media relationships.

We build the strategy as operators who will also run it. Every recommendation ends in a channel plan our PR, KOL, content and partnership specialists can execute, sequenced along Test → Win → Scale: prove traction in Germany, win with the right channel mix, then expand to Austria, Switzerland and, through our network, France, Spain and Italy. Our guide explains how to enter the German crypto market step by step.

What you get:
- Market and competitor analysis: Who already wins in your category across DACH, how they position themselves, which channels and keywords they own and where the openings are for an international brand.
- Positioning and narratives: A positioning for the German market and a small set of core narratives that match local expectations on trust, security and regulation, turned into messaging your team can use.
- Audience fit: Prioritized segments of German-speaking users, from first-time buyers to experienced traders, with the questions, objections and trust signals each segment needs before it signs up.
- Regulatory-readiness check: A marketing checklist covering MiCA, BaFin expectations and ad-platform rules, reviewed together with your legal counsel. We flag what needs clarifying; your lawyers give the legal advice.
- Channel mix and sequencing: Which channels to start with – PR, KOLs, content and SEO, partnerships, community – in which order and with which budget logic, structured along Test → Win → Scale.
- KPIs and launch roadmap: A roadmap with milestones, owners and KPIs for each phase, plus a reporting setup that shows which channels drive sign-ups and which ones to cut.

How we work:
1. Discovery: We map your product, goals, current traction and constraints: licenses, markets you already serve, team capacity and what has or hasn't worked elsewhere in Europe. Then we agree on the decision the strategy has to support. (Output: brief and success criteria)
2. Market and competitor analysis: We analyze German competitors, search demand, media and creator coverage and comparison platforms in your category, and identify where an international brand can credibly win attention and trust. (Output: market map and gap analysis)
3. Positioning and readiness: We define positioning, narratives and audience priorities and run the regulatory-readiness check with your legal counsel, so claims, disclaimers and onboarding flows are ready for German users. (Output: positioning paper and readiness checklist)
4. Channel plan and roadmap: We choose the channel mix, sequence it along Test → Win → Scale, set KPIs for each phase and define the first campaigns with clear owners, assets and reporting. (Output: launch roadmap and KPI framework)
5. Launch and iterate: Our specialists execute the plan or support your team. We review results against the KPIs, shift budget to the channels that perform and prepare the expansion to Austria, Switzerland and beyond. (Output: live campaigns and performance reviews)

Showcase (Waltio): Waltio, the French crypto tax tool with 150,000+ users, set out to establish itself among Germany's leading crypto tax providers – in a market held by local incumbents with a decade of brand, SEO and industry relationships. We built and ran the German go-to-market, timed around tax-season demand and split into four workstreams: SEO, launch PR, partnerships and owned content. Read the full Waltio case study.

FAQ:
Q: What does a crypto go-to-market strategy for Germany include?
A: It covers market and competitor analysis, positioning and narratives for German-speaking users, audience priorities, a regulatory-readiness check with your legal counsel, the channel mix and its sequencing, KPIs and a launch roadmap. At MarketWerk the strategy is built to be executed: every recommendation turns into concrete PR, KOL, content, partnership or community activities with owners and metrics.

Q: Do we need a German entity or license to market in Germany?
A: It depends on what you offer and how you are authorized. Under MiCA, crypto-asset service providers authorized in one EU member state can passport their services to Germany and Austria. Switzerland is outside MiCA and supervised by FINMA, and some products fall outside MiCA altogether. We are not lawyers: we work through these questions with your legal counsel before launch and align all marketing with the outcome.

Q: Is DACH one market?
A: No. Germany and Austria are EU members under MiCA, supervised by BaFin and the FMA. Switzerland is neither in the EU nor under MiCA and is supervised by FINMA. The tax treatment of private crypto gains differs between all three, and so do media, creators and language nuances. We usually start in Germany as the largest market and adapt messaging and channels from there. See our DACH market comparison.

Q: Can we start with one channel?
A: Yes, and often that is the right test. We pick the channel with the clearest path to your first KPI – for example SEO content in a category with strong search intent, or creator explainers for a product that needs education. PR, partnerships or community follow once the signal is clear. Winning usually takes several channels working together, not one channel alone.

Q: How do you measure success?
A: We agree on KPIs for each phase before launch. In the test phase they are leading indicators such as qualified traffic, search visibility, media coverage and sign-up conversion; in the win and scale phases they are users, revenue and acquisition cost by channel. Regular reporting shows what works and where we shift budget. We don't promise numbers we can't control.

## PR & Media – https://marketwerk.com/services/crypto-pr-agency-germany/
Launch PR, press releases written natively in German and story angles that crypto, finance and tech editors actually pick up – plus clearly labelled sponsored placements where they make sense.

At a glance:
- MarketWerk is a crypto PR agency for international crypto brands that want media coverage in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
- The service covers launch PR, press releases written natively in German, spokesperson positioning, newsjacking around MiCA and tax season, clearly labelled sponsored placements and reputation basics.
- MarketWerk's launch PR campaign for Waltio's German market entry generated 70+ media publications, including a placement on the Handelsblatt press portal.

A crypto PR agency for Germany gets your brand into the media German-speaking users trust – and makes sure what appears there is accurate, compliant and worth reading. That takes press releases written in German, story angles with local relevance and direct pitching to editors in crypto, finance and tech.

The media landscape is broader than crypto news. Specialist outlets such as BTC-ECHO and Cointelegraph Deutsch sit next to business and finance media like Handelsblatt and finanzen.net, tech media like t3n, Der Brutkasten and Trending Topics in Austria and finews.ch in Switzerland. Each has its own audience and its own idea of news. A translated global press release rarely makes it into any of them.

German editors look for substance: what changes for users in Germany, how your product handles security and regulation, and why the story matters now. We build PR around those questions, time it around moments like MiCA milestones or tax season and connect it with KOL campaigns and SEO content, so coverage keeps working after the news cycle. Our crypto PR guide for Germany covers the media side in detail.

What you get:
- PR strategy and story angles: A PR plan built on angles that work locally: impact for German users, security, regulation, data you can share and founder perspectives – each mapped to the outlets and formats that fit.
- Native German press releases: Releases written in German from the start, not translated: local news value, correct financial and regulatory terms, quotes that sound natural and a boilerplate that holds up to editorial scrutiny.
- Media relations and pitching: Targeted pitching to editors and journalists in German-speaking crypto, finance and tech media, with a tailored angle per outlet, follow-ups and coordination of interviews and background briefings.
- Spokesperson positioning: Preparation for your spokespeople: the topics they can credibly own in Germany, key messages, tough questions on regulation and security, and language support for German-speaking interviews.
- Newsjacking and commentary: Fast, well-sourced commentary when regulation, market events or tax season put crypto in the news, so your brand shows up where readers look for context, not only for announcements.
- Sponsored placements and reputation: Clearly labelled sponsored articles where earned media won't reach far enough, plus media monitoring and reputation basics: consistent facts, a press kit and prepared answers to critical questions.

How we work:
1. Story audit: We review your product, data, milestones and spokespeople and find what is genuinely newsworthy in Germany. We also flag claims that need a legal check under MiCA or advertising rules before anything is pitched. (Output: story map and claims check)
2. Media plan: We match each story to the right outlets and formats – news, interviews, guest articles, commentary – across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and decide where a labelled sponsored placement adds reach. (Output: media list and PR calendar)
3. Content and pitching: We write the German press materials, prepare your spokespeople and pitch editors individually. Launch news, follow-up stories and commentary are spaced out so coverage builds over time instead of peaking once. (Output: press releases, press kit and pitches)
4. Coverage and amplification: We track publications, secure backlinks where possible and pass the strongest coverage to KOL, content and partnership channels, so it reaches users and doesn't end up only in a clipping report. (Output: coverage report with reach and links)

Showcase (Waltio): When Waltio, the French crypto tax tool with 150,000+ users, entered Germany, local incumbents had spent a decade building media relationships. We ran the launch PR campaign around the German market entry and timed coverage with tax-season demand, so readers met Waltio when they were actively looking for a solution. PR worked hand in hand with SEO, partnerships and creator content. See the full Waltio case.

FAQ:
Q: Which media do you target in Germany, Austria and Switzerland?
A: It depends on the story and the audience. Typical targets include crypto media such as BTC-ECHO and Cointelegraph Deutsch, business and finance media such as Handelsblatt and finanzen.net, tech media such as t3n, Der Brutkasten and Trending Topics in Austria and finews.ch in Switzerland. We pitch every outlet individually and don't claim exclusive media partnerships with any of them.

Q: Do you promise a fixed number of articles?
A: No. Earned coverage depends on editorial decisions, so a fixed number of articles can't honestly be promised. We commit to the work: strong angles, native German materials and persistent, targeted pitching. Where reach has to be predictable, we recommend sponsored placements – always clearly labelled as advertising, as German media law and MiCA's rules on marketing communications require.

Q: Do you write press releases in German?
A: Yes – natively, not as translations. German editors notice translated copy immediately: awkward phrasing, wrong financial terms and angles that only matter outside Germany. We write releases, quotes and boilerplates in German from the start, adapt them for Austria and Switzerland where needed and can provide an English version for internal approval.

Q: How does MiCA affect crypto PR?
A: MiCA requires marketing communications about crypto-assets to be clearly identifiable as marketing, fair, clear and not misleading, and consistent with the white paper where one is required. Editorial coverage is the journalist's responsibility, but your press releases, quotes and sponsored content are your communication. We align claims with your legal counsel. Our MiCA marketing guide explains the rules. This is not legal advice.

Q: Do you work with token projects, exchanges or DeFi protocols?
A: We work with crypto brands such as Waltio, ether.fi, Blever, Nest Collective and Anon Summit, and we decide on new projects case by case. What matters is a product we can credibly explain to German media and users, and a regulatory position your counsel has reviewed. We don't promote projects that rely on price promises.

## KOL & Influencers – https://marketwerk.com/services/crypto-influencer-marketing/
We find, vet and brief German-speaking crypto creators on YouTube, X, Instagram, Telegram and podcasts – for campaigns that educate, convert and are clearly labelled as advertising.

At a glance:
- MarketWerk runs crypto influencer and KOL marketing for international crypto brands that want to reach German-speaking users in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
- The service covers creator vetting and audience-quality checks, briefing, ad labelling and MiCA-consistent claims, formats such as explainers and series, tracking and long-term ambassador programs.
- For Waltio's German launch, MarketWerk combined YouTube explainers, creator content with MissCrypto on X and Instagram and Waltio's own German YouTube channel – part of a launch that reached 1M+ impressions across channels.

Crypto influencer marketing in Germany works when the right German-speaking creators explain your product to an audience that trusts them – clearly labelled, accurate and repeated often enough to stick. In DACH, that trust comes from education, not hype: users want to understand fees, security and regulation before they sign up.

The creator scene is smaller than in English-speaking markets, and audience quality varies widely. Some channels have real, engaged communities in DACH; others have inflated follower counts or audiences that sit mostly outside the region. Paid posts must be labelled as "Werbung" or "Anzeige" under German unfair competition and media law, and claims about crypto-assets have to stay fair, clear and not misleading under MiCA. Picking creators on reach alone is the fastest way to waste a budget here.

We know this side from the inside: our founder Michael Beches built a German crypto YouTube community with thousands of followers himself. We vet creators on audience data rather than follower counts, favor series and tutorials over one-off posts and connect creator content with PR and your community. Our guide to crypto influencer marketing in Germany goes deeper.

What you get:
- Creator scouting and vetting: A shortlist of German-speaking creators on YouTube, X, Instagram, Telegram and podcasts, checked for topic fit, tone, past sponsorships and how they handled earlier crypto partnerships.
- Audience-quality checks: We review audience location and language, engagement patterns, comment quality and signs of bought followers, so your budget reaches real German-speaking users instead of inflated numbers.
- Briefs and compliance: Briefs with key messages, mandatory disclosures and claims to avoid: labelling as "Werbung" or "Anzeige", no promises of returns and statements consistent with your white paper and legal guidance.
- Formats that educate: Explainers, tutorials, walkthroughs and multi-part series that show how your product works in practice. In our experience, German audiences reward useful content far more than one-off shout-outs.
- Tracking and reporting: Tracking links, codes and landing pages per creator, so we can compare reach, clicks, sign-ups and cost per result and move budget to the creators who actually perform.
- Long-term ambassadors: Ambassador programs with your best-performing creators: recurring content, product feedback and a familiar face for your brand in the German-speaking crypto community.

How we work:
1. Goals and audience: We define who you want to reach, what they need to understand before signing up and which actions count as success: sign-ups, app installs, deposits or qualified traffic. That decides which creators and platforms make sense. (Output: campaign goals and target audience)
2. Scouting and vetting: We build a longlist of German-speaking creators, check audience quality and past brand deals and narrow it down to a shortlist that fits your product, budget and risk profile. (Output: vetted creator shortlist)
3. Briefing and compliance: We negotiate terms, write the briefs and agree on formats, disclosures and claims. Scripts or key points are checked against your legal guidance before anything is published. (Output: signed briefs and approved key messages)
4. Launch and tracking: Creators publish on a coordinated schedule, ideally as a series rather than a single post. We monitor comments and questions, feed them back to your team and track every creator separately. (Output: live content and tracking dashboard)
5. Optimize and retain: We compare results by creator and format, drop what doesn't perform and turn the strongest partnerships into long-term ambassador relationships with recurring content and direct product feedback. (Output: performance report and ambassador plan)

Showcase (Waltio): Crypto taxes are a topic people need explained, not advertised. For Waltio's German launch, we combined YouTube influencer explainers with creator content from MissCrypto on X and Instagram and ran weekly videos on Waltio's own German YouTube channel, with German tax experts answering questions on camera. When tax season peaked, content went out almost daily across channels. Read the Waltio case.

FAQ:
Q: How do you choose German crypto influencers?
A: We start with fit, not reach: does the creator cover your topic credibly, and does their audience match your target users? Then we check audience location and language, engagement quality, comment sections, past sponsorships and red flags such as bought followers or promotion of questionable projects. Only creators who pass make the shortlist, and you approve the final selection.

Q: Do influencer posts need to be labelled in Germany?
A: Yes. Paid or otherwise commercially motivated posts must be clearly recognizable as advertising, typically labelled "Werbung" or "Anzeige", under German unfair competition law (UWG) and media law. Similar principles apply in Austria and Switzerland. For crypto-assets, MiCA adds that marketing must be fair, clear and not misleading. We build both into every brief. This is not legal advice.

Q: Which platforms work best for crypto KOL marketing in DACH?
A: It depends on your product. YouTube suits explainers and tutorials when users need to understand a product before they trust it. X is where the crypto-native audience discusses news and projects, Instagram reaches a broader and less crypto-native audience, and Telegram groups and podcasts build depth with smaller, loyal communities. Most campaigns combine two or three platforms instead of spreading thin.

Q: Why series instead of one-off posts?
A: One sponsored post rarely changes behavior, especially in a market where users need trust before they sign up. A series – for example a tutorial, a follow-up with results and a Q&A – gives the audience time to understand the product and see the creator actually use it. It also gives us enough data to judge whether a creator works for you.

Q: How do you measure influencer campaigns?
A: Every creator gets their own tracking links or codes, and we report reach, engagement, clicks, sign-ups and cost per result side by side. Views alone say little; what matters is what happens after the click. Comments and questions from the audience are the second signal, because they show which messages land and which need work.

## Content & SEO – https://marketwerk.com/services/crypto-content-seo-localization/
German keyword research, SEO content your audience is searching for and localization that gets tone, terms and trust signals right – plus owned channels that keep working after launch.

At a glance:
- MarketWerk provides crypto SEO, content and localization for international crypto brands that need German-language content for Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
- The service covers German keyword research, SEO guides, calculators and blog content, localization of tone, legal and tax terms and trust signals, website and app localization QA and owned channels such as YouTube and newsletters.
- For Waltio, MarketWerk built an SEO foundation of 4 main guides, 2 tax calculators and 10 blog posts; within a few months, Waltio reached #3 in organic keyword rankings for crypto tax topics.

Crypto SEO for Germany means ranking for the terms German-speaking users actually type – and then convincing them with content that reads as if it were written in Germany. Translation alone rarely gets you there. German users search with different terms, often expect more detail and judge your brand by how precise your language is.

Good crypto localization for German audiences starts with decisions. Do you address users with the informal "du" or the formal "Sie"? Do you write "Haltefrist" and "Spekulationsfrist", or translate "holding period" literally? Which trust signals matter most – regulation, fee transparency, security, German-language support? Swiss readers expect "ss" instead of "ß" and prices in CHF, and Austrian German has its own vocabulary.

We build your content engine around those answers: German keyword research, guides and calculators that solve real questions, blog content, owned channels like YouTube and newsletters, and QA for your website and app. The goal is a repeatable process, not a one-time translation project. The same content then feeds your PR and creator campaigns. Our guide to crypto localization for the German market goes into detail.

What you get:
- German keyword research: Keyword and topic research in German for your category: search terms, questions and intent across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, prioritized by relevance, competition and closeness to sign-up.
- SEO content that answers questions: Main guides, comparison and explainer pages, calculators and blog posts built around real search intent, with clean structure, internal linking and updates in time for seasonal peaks.
- Localization beyond translation: Tone of voice, the du/Sie decision, correct legal and tax terminology and local trust signals – applied to messaging, landing pages, emails and in-product copy.
- Website and app localization QA: A review of your German website and app: wording, terminology, date and number formats, legal pages, onboarding and support texts, plus a list of fixes ranked by impact.
- Owned channels: A German YouTube channel, newsletter or blog that builds an audience you own, with formats like expert Q&As and tutorials that also feed SEO, PR and creator campaigns.
- A repeatable content engine: An editorial calendar, briefs, a style guide and a glossary, so new content keeps the same quality and terminology – whether we produce it or your in-house team does.

How we work:
1. Research and audit: We research German search demand in your category, analyze who ranks today and audit your existing German website, app and content for terminology, tone and gaps that cost you trust or traffic. (Output: keyword map and content audit)
2. Localization framework: We set the foundations: tone of voice, du or Sie, a glossary of legal, tax and product terms, the trust signals to show and the differences to cover for Austria and Switzerland. (Output: style guide and glossary)
3. Foundation content: We create the core assets first – main guides, calculators or tools and the first blog posts – timed ahead of the moments when your audience searches most, such as tax season. (Output: published SEO foundation)
4. Content engine and owned channels: We set up the editorial calendar and owned channels like YouTube or a newsletter, measure rankings, traffic and conversions, keep updating what performs and expand topics that show potential. (Output: editorial calendar and SEO reporting)

Showcase (Waltio): Waltio entered a German crypto tax market where incumbents had a decade-long SEO head start. We built evergreen German-language content ahead of tax season: 4 main guides, 2 tax calculators and 10 blog posts. Alongside it, Waltio's own German YouTube channel published weekly videos with German tax experts on camera. Within a few months, Waltio reached #3 in organic keyword rankings for crypto tax topics. Read the Waltio case.

FAQ:
Q: Isn't a good translation enough for the German market?
A: Usually not. A translation converts words; localization adapts the message. German users search with different terms, expect precise legal and tax language and look for trust signals such as regulation, fee transparency and German-language support. Literal translations of product and tax terms also miss the keywords people actually use. That's why we start from German search data and write for German readers.

Q: How long does crypto SEO in Germany take to show results?
A: It depends on your category, your competitors and the state of your site, so we don't promise rankings or timelines. What we can show is how it went for Waltio: in a market where incumbents had a decade-long SEO head start, Waltio reached #3 in organic keyword rankings for crypto tax topics within a few months. Here is how we plan content around tax season.

Q: Should we address German users with du or Sie?
A: It depends on your brand and audience. Many crypto and fintech brands in Germany use the informal du because it feels direct and modern, while more traditional financial brands keep the formal Sie. What matters most is consistency across website, app, emails and support. We make the decision with you early and document it in the style guide.

Q: Do you localize for Austria and Switzerland too?
A: Yes, where it makes a difference. Most German content works across DACH, but details differ: Swiss Standard German uses "ss" instead of "ß", prices may need to be shown in CHF, Austrian German has its own vocabulary, and regulation and tax rules differ – Switzerland is not under MiCA. We flag where a separate page or version is worth it, for example for tax or regulatory topics.

Q: Can you work with our in-house team?
A: Yes. We can produce everything, or provide research, a style guide and editing while your own team writes. We adapt to your setup and leave behind a glossary, briefs and an editorial calendar, so the content engine keeps running with or without us. For tax and regulatory topics, we set up a shared review process with your experts.

## Partnerships – https://marketwerk.com/services/crypto-partnerships-affiliates/
We get your brand listed, reviewed and recommended where German-speaking users compare crypto products – through comparison platforms, crypto portals, affiliates, co-marketing and events.

At a glance:
- MarketWerk builds partnerships and affiliate programs for international crypto brands entering Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
- The service covers comparison platforms and crypto portals, affiliate partners, co-marketing with exchanges, wallets and fintechs, event presence and partner-driven discovery and backlinks.
- For Waltio, MarketWerk set up partnerships with crypto and comparison sites such as Bitcoin2Go, Bitcoin-Kurier and MissCrypto, and Waltio reached Top 3 rankings on selected comparison platforms.

Crypto partnerships in Germany put your product where German-speaking users already research and compare: comparison platforms, crypto portals, trusted creators, exchanges, wallets and fintechs. In a market with a high trust threshold, a recommendation from an established local name often counts for more than any ad you could run.

Paid reach is limited anyway. Major ad platforms restrict crypto advertising and require authorization in many EU markets, which makes partners one of the few channels that scale. Comparison sites and portals also deliver what SEO needs: backlinks and discovery from sites search engines already trust. Affiliate and co-marketing deals follow the same rules as your own marketing – labelled, fair, clear and not misleading.

We build these partnerships hands-on: identifying the partners that matter in your category, negotiating listings, affiliate terms and co-marketing, and planning event presence – our founder co-founded Germany's largest blockchain conference. Partnerships work best alongside PR and SEO content. Once Germany works, our network in France, Spain and Italy helps you take the next step. Our DACH market comparison shows how Germany, Austria and Switzerland differ.

What you get:
- Partner map and shortlist: An overview of the comparison platforms, crypto portals, affiliates, creators and co-marketing partners that matter for your category in DACH, prioritized by audience fit, traffic quality and SEO value.
- Comparison platforms and portals: Listings, reviews and rankings on German crypto comparison sites and portals. We prepare the product data, fee and security information and trust signals these platforms and their readers check.

# Guides
## How to enter the German crypto market: a go-to-market playbook for 2026 – https://marketwerk.com/blog/enter-german-crypto-market/
Key takeaways:
- Germany is Europe's largest economy and one of its biggest crypto markets, and its demanding users and strict regulation make it a strong test case for any European rollout.
- Regulatory groundwork comes first: clarify your MiCA status with legal counsel before any campaign targets German users.
- Localization beats translation: German-speaking users expect German-language support, transparent fees and clear answers on security and regulation.
- Crypto market entry in Germany works as a system of PR, KOLs, content, partnerships and community, sequenced from Test to Win to Scale.

To enter the German crypto market, you need three things before you scale spend: a clear regulatory footing under MiCA, a product and message localized for German-speaking users, and a channel mix that builds trust step by step. Germany rewards crypto brands that show up in German, explain instead of hype and stay consistent for months. This playbook lays out the sequence we use for crypto market entry in Germany: Test → Win → Scale.

## Why start with Germany

Germany is Europe's largest economy and one of its biggest crypto markets. Together with Austria and Switzerland, it gives you 100M+ German speakers across DACH – one language and a shared media and creator scene.

The stronger argument is difficulty. In our experience, German-speaking users are privacy-conscious, read the fine print and prefer regulated providers with German-language support and transparent fees. Add strict regulation, and Germany becomes a demanding proving ground: if your go-to-market works here, it works across Europe.

## Regulatory groundwork before the first campaign

The EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA, Regulation (EU) 2023/1114(https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1114/oj)) has applied in full since 30 December 2024, and BaFin(https://www.bafin.de) is the competent authority in Germany. Before targeting German users, clarify four points with legal counsel:

- **Your status:** Do you need authorization as a crypto-asset service provider (CASP) – from BaFin, or from another EU authority and passported into Germany? Does your token offer or listing require a white paper?
- **Your claims:** Marketing must be clearly identifiable, fair, clear and not misleading, and consistent with the white paper – on every landing page, creator brief and press release.
- **Your paid channels:** Major ad platforms restrict crypto ads. Google, for example, requires MiCA authorization for many crypto ads in the EU.
- **Your DACH footprint:** Austria also applies MiCA, supervised by the FMA(https://www.fma.gv.at). Switzerland is outside the EU and MiCA; its regulator is FINMA(https://www.finma.ch).

Our guide to MiCA marketing rules covers the marketing side in detail.

*This section is general information, not legal advice. Work with qualified legal counsel on your setup.*

## Positioning and localization: translation is not enough

Global positioning rarely survives the trip to Germany unchanged. Start with the competition: who already owns your category in German search, media and creator channels, and which narrative is still open? For Waltio, the picture was a market held by local incumbents with a decade of brand, SEO and industry relationships.

Localization then turns positioning into something German users trust:

- **Language:** native German copy across website, onboarding, support and legal pages.
- **Proof points:** regulatory status, security, fee transparency and who is responsible.
- **Formats:** guides, explainers and tools built around real German search terms.
- **Tone:** factual and specific. Hype costs credibility here and creates regulatory risk.

More in our article on localizing a crypto brand for German speakers.

## Channel mix and sequencing: Test → Win → Scale

No single channel carries a German launch. What works is the right mix, launched fast and working together:

| Channel | Role in market entry | Typical first move |
|---|---|---|
| PR & media | Third-party credibility, backlinks, branded search | A launch story with a local angle |
| KOLs & creators | Reach and trust through education | An explainer series with German creators |
| Content & SEO | Demand capture that compounds | German guides for real search questions |
| Partnerships | Discovery and backlinks | Placements on crypto and comparison sites |
| Community | Retention, support and feedback | A moderated German-language channel |

The channels feed each other: creator videos trigger searches, searches land on German guides, and media coverage makes the brand look established. Our guides to crypto PR in Germany and choosing KOLs that convert go deeper.

### Test

Validate positioning and messages with real German-speaking users: a few creator collaborations, the first German guides, a launch story. Track which messages produce signups, not just clicks. The goal is one answer: is there product-market fit in Germany?

### Win

Double down on what worked and run the channels together. Timing matters: a tax product builds content before tax season and peaks with it; an exchange or wallet can pair a feature launch with regulation news.

### Scale

Once Germany works, extend to Austria and Switzerland with local media, creators and regulatory checks – our DACH market comparison shows where the markets differ. Then adapt the playbook for France, Spain and Italy, where our network lets campaigns launch right away.

## How to measure progress

Measure what proves traction in Germany, not what flatters a report:

- **Demand:** branded search from Germany and rankings for German keywords.
- **Conversion:** signups, verified accounts and first transactions from DACH, by channel and creator.
- **Credibility:** media publications, German-language backlinks, positions on comparison platforms.
- **Efficiency:** cost per onboarded user and the messages that convert best.

Set a baseline before launch and review it monthly. Impressions and follower counts are context, not proof.

## Common mistakes when entering Germany

- **Translating instead of localizing.** English-only support and hype-heavy copy tell German users the product was not built for them.
- **One big influencer instead of a system.** A single shout-out creates a spike, not trust; creator series backed by content and PR build lasting demand.
- **Ignoring tax season.** It shifts attention and search demand every year – publish German content ahead of it, not during it.
- **Treating regulation as an afterthought.** Campaigns pulled after legal review burn budget and trust; build compliance into every brief.
